clue.text: Add finishing touch that's sometimes displayed on car

definitions.meaning: to top everything off, crown the whole business
a learner driver's car shows a big red L, a capital letter L

explanation.surface: Advice on putting the final flourish on a car, perhaps a badge or trim.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer differently: CAPITAL L, the letter on a British learner driver's L-plate.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means crowning everything, and an L-plate on a learner's vehicle shows an upper-case letter L.

clue.text: Hardy or Scott, for example

parts.note: not the writers: Hardy commanded Nelson's flagship Victory and Scott led a polar expedition, both naval rank-holders

explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hardy and Walter Scott are novelists, but here it is Nelson's Hardy and Scott of the Antarctic.
explanation.definitionFit: Both men held the naval rank of ship's commander.

clue.text: Canvassed views

parts.note: not opinions sought by canvassing: scenes put on canvas by an artist

explanation.definitionFit: Landscapes or scenes rendered in oil on canvas are artworks of this kind.

clue.text: So a tree bursts into flower

indicators.note: bursts says the letters of so a tree break apart and reform

explanation.surface: A tree is blossoming spectacularly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bursts into flower' reads as blooming; 'bursts' is the anagram signal, 'flower' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid rose scented like tea is a garden bloom.

clue.text: Sort of officer helping to coordinate union

definitions.text: Sort of officer helping to coordinate
definitions.meaning: an officer whose job is linking departments or groups
an affair or close connection between two people

explanation.definitionFit: Such an officer links organisations, and the word also means an intimate relationship.

clue.text: An import without purpose

parts.note: the import or drift of a remark is its general meaning

explanation.surface: An imported item seems to serve no function at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone drifting with no aim or direction is said to be at sea, aimless.

clue.text: Frightfully impressed with card-player in a fight

indicators.note: in says the card-player goes inside a word for fight

parts.note: a ruck is a scrum or brawl
West is one of the four players at bridge

explanation.surface: Someone dazzled by a gambler during a scuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of wonder mixed with fear, as one is before something overwhelming.

clue.text: Managed to continue providing capital

parts.note: to manage a business is to run it
go on means continue

explanation.surface: Someone kept going while supplying money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money but is the city, the former capital of Burma.
explanation.definitionFit: The city, now Yangon, was formerly Burma's seat of government.

clue.text: Strategy taking advantage of King's position, perhaps

definitions.text: Strategy taking advantage of King's position, perhaps

parts.words: Strategy taking advantage of King's position, perhaps
parts.note: in bridge, leading towards a card so a higher card is captured or bypassed depending on where an opponent's king sits

explanation.definitionFit: A bridge play exploiting where opponents hold key cards, also more generally subtle skill.

clue.text: At first sight, minimal change for us if America changes

parts.note: the smallest British coin is a penny, abbreviated p

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the words if and America are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A note that little would alter for Britons if the United States altered course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges IF AMERICA into RIMAFACIE, after P, the penny; 'for us' marks that coin as British.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is used in law for evidence that looks sufficient on its face, before closer inspection.

clue.text: Novel pet for Wendy

definitions.meaning: a novel by Emile Zola about a courtesan
in Peter Pan the Darling children, Wendy among them, have a Newfoundland dog as nursemaid

explanation.definitionFit: Zola's book carries this title, and the same name belongs to the nursery dog in J M Barrie's play.

clue.text: Put in suits in order to get ready

indicators.note: in says the word for put goes inside the word for suits

parts.note: lawsuits are actions at law
to station something is to put it in position

explanation.surface: Getting dressed properly in business suits so as to be prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put in suits' reads like dressing up; actually STATION goes in ACTIONS, lawsuits.
explanation.definitionFit: The military order tells troops to take their posts and prepare for battle.

clue.text: Girl eager to get stuff from Chinatown, initially

parts.note: Nan is a girl's name, short for Ann
keen means eager

explanation.surface: A girl is keen to buy fabric in Chinatown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuff' here is cloth: the yellowish cotton was first made in Nanking, China, hence 'from Chinatown, initially'.
explanation.definitionFit: The cotton fabric takes its name from Nanking, where it was originally woven.

clue.text: Put out of hostel, I'm in a tent a bit

indicators.note: a bit says only a part of the words hostel, I'm in a tent is taken

explanation.surface: Someone thrown out of a hostel ends up camping in a tent.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts with the last two letters of 'hostel' and stops two letters into 'tent'.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock a competitor out of a contest is to remove them.

clue.text: Carpenter's trees

definitions.meaning: Peter Quince is the carpenter in A Midsummer Night's Dream, so this is his possessive
fruit trees bearing hard yellow pear-like fruit

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's carpenter is named Quince, and the orchard trees with aromatic yellow fruit share that name.

clue.text: State with force — evil's to be overthrown in this theology

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

indicators.note: in says the turned word goes inside the word for force

parts.note: vim is energy or force

indicators.note: overthrown says the word for evil is turned upside down, read backwards in a down clue

parts.note: sin is evil; evil's means evil is

explanation.surface: A preacher declaring that wickedness must be forcefully toppled under this creed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be overthrown' turns SIN into NIS, which goes in VIM.
explanation.definitionFit: The Protestant doctrine of John Calvin stresses predestination.

clue.text: It's said foolishly in row, to show contempt

indicators.note: in says the jumbled letters go inside the word for row

parts.note: a din is a noisy row

indicators.note: foolishly says the letters of said are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something said stupidly during an argument signals scorn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolishly' turns SAID into ISDA, which sits in DIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorn is to treat someone or something as unworthy, looking down on them.

clue.text: Naughty child a head appears to accuse

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
a head, as in a pound a head, means each

explanation.surface: A mischievous child seems to be pointing the finger.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge a public official formally with misconduct.

clue.text: Giant does, nonetheless, get married

indicators.note: read as none-less, meaning take away nothing, the letter O, from the word does

parts.note: to pair is to mate or marry

explanation.surface: A giant marries anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: Giant Despair is the ogre of Doubting Castle in Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunyan's allegory names its giant after hopelessness.

clue.text: Cake butcher put in frying-pan

indicators.note: put in says the word for butcher goes inside the word for cake

parts.note: to cake is to harden or set
to butcher is to kill

explanation.surface: A cake made by a butcher is placed in the frying-pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cake' is a verb, to set hard; 'butcher' a verb, to kill.
explanation.definitionFit: A skillet is a heavy, long-handled pan for frying.

clue.text: Lines composed in Staines

indicators.note: composed says the letters of Staines are put together anew

explanation.surface: Verses written in Staines, a town near London.
explanation.walkthrough: Staines is a town west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A poem of six six-line stanzas plus an envoi, so a set of verse lines.

clue.text: Is love overdue for such a loner?

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
late means overdue

explanation.surface: Asking whether a delayed romance suits a solitary person.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means someone set apart from society, a recluse.

clue.text: Superman's sounding tense

indicators.note: sounding says the word for superman is said aloud

parts.note: a titan is a superman, a giant of strength; the 's means is

explanation.surface: Superman's voice sounds strained.
explanation.definitionFit: To make taut or stiffen, the verb sense of tense.

clue.text: Such inspiration among Virginia's devotees isn't healthy for others

definitions.text: Such inspiration among Virginia's devotees isn't healthy for others

parts.words: Such inspiration among Virginia's devotees isn't healthy for others
parts.note: Virginia is tobacco; its devotees are smokers, and the inspiration is breathing in, which harms bystanders who inhale it

explanation.walkthrough: Virginia is a tobacco, not a woman, and 'inspiration' is literally breathing in.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-smokers inhaling others' tobacco fumes are harmed involuntarily, which is the health concern described.

clue.text: Old man leading a cultural movement

indicators.note: leading means the word for old man comes before a

parts.note: old man is slang for father, dad

explanation.surface: An elderly man heads an artistic movement.
explanation.definitionFit: The anti-art avant-garde movement began in Zurich during the First World War.

clue.text: Continental expert is caught in a frantic disturbance

indicators.note: caught in says is goes inside the rearranged letters
disturbance says the letters of a frantic are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A specialist is trapped in a frenzied commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbance' makes AFRICANT of A FRANTIC; 'caught in' puts IS in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar of Africa's languages and cultures, Africa being a continent.

clue.text: Storm damage

definitions.meaning: to storm a position is to rush at it in attack
informally the damage is the cost, as in what's the damage?

explanation.definitionFit: Troops rush an enemy in an attack, and a fee or price is the colloquial damage.

clue.text: Traveller reportedly takes sea route to island

indicators.note: reportedly says the word for taking a sea route is heard, not seen

parts.note: to sail is to travel by sea
the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A voyager is said to go by sea to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: A travelling salesman is the traveller; the Isle of Man is a British island.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial traveller is a rep who journeys round selling goods.
